unmapped_findings: For the 15Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 3 h, the only condition-specific quantitative datum reported is the Vickers hardness (938.2 ± 18.0 HV, Table 2); no EBSD/SEM/TEM micrograph panel exists for this exact condition — the 15Al characterizations were performed at 525 °C/3 h, 550 °C/6 h and 650 °C/3 h (EBSD Fig. 4), the SEM matrix of Fig. 7 covers 525/550/575 °C (1,3,6,10 h) plus 600 °C-1 h, 600 °C-6 h, 625 °C-1 h and 650 °C-1 h, and the TEM study (Fig. 11) was on the 15Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 6 h (the peak-hardness 965.6 HV condition).

For the 15Al alloy, the optimal aging temperature range for achieving ultra-high hardness was reported as mainly 525 °C–600 °C, and the aging-hardening kinetic/structural trends at 600 °C and above (near-complete α→β-Mn transformation within ~1 h with fine BCC and FCC precipitates) are the general context within which the 600 °C/3 h state sits; the samples' peak hardness 965.6 HV is reached at 600 °C/6 h (a different aging condition / sibling sample).
